Lazy data frames

Source: R/lazy-dataframe.R
lazy-dataframe.Rd

A lazy obs or var is a LazyDFrame, an S4Vectors::DataFrame whose columns are lazy (see lazy-columns). Reading it reads metadata, the categories and (with load_annotation_index) the index. Row subsetting, column subsetting and printing work as for any DataFrame and stay lazy, and lazy_dataframe_realise() gives the DataFrame that read_h5ad()/read_zarr() give for the same Element.

Usage

lazy_dataframe(
  store,
  path,
  load_annotation_index = TRUE,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

# S4 method for class 'LazyDFrame,ANY'
extractROWS(x, i)

# S4 method for class 'LazyDFrame'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

lazy_dataframe_realise(df, call = rlang::caller_env())

Arguments

store

An open store handle, see io-store.

path

Absolute path of the dataframe Element.

load_annotation_index

Whether the index is read into memory.

call

The call reported by errors.

x

A LazyDFrame.

i

Row positions, already normalised by S4Vectors.

df

A LazyDFrame.

Details

With load_annotation_index = FALSE the row names are NULL (Python's dummy range index) and the index stays a lazy column in the lazy_index slot, which row subsetting follows and realising loads.
